title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Notational overload: the PGL2-torsor Isom(P^1(C)_{X^an}, P) is written P^an, though the same symbol is used for the P^1-bundle itself. It should be 𝒞^an. This is a slip, not a mathematical error.
In 'U^an × P^an_x' the fibre should be P_x, the fibre at x, not a bundle. Minor.

The identification of sections disjoint from σ with connections on ω (rather than on some twist L) depends on the normalisation chosen for P. The next page corrects/refines this via L with L^2 ≅ ω^3. The draft is internally consistent once that is taken into account.

ideas.what: Projective structure on a curve as a P^1-bundle with flat connection and a nowhere-horizontal section, equivalent to a projective atlas (torsor of local charts under PGL2), proved via GAGA.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1967, indigenous bundles, analytic); Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, 1990s); Drinfeld–Sokolov (1985)

ideas.what: P = 𝒞/B with σ as B-reduction. Local horizontal sections of P are sections of 𝒰/B, i.e. local affine structures compatible with the projective structure.
ideas.modern_name: Oper as G-bundle with flat connection and generic B-reduction; affine structures subordinate to a projective structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (affine/projective connections on Riemann surfaces); Beilinson–Drinfeld

ideas.what: Sections of P disjoint from σ correspond to connections D on ω, and horizontality means c_D = c_0, the induced projective connection.
ideas.modern_name: Affine connections inducing a given projective connection (Schwarzian / Riccati relation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Gunning, Tyurin); algebraic version: Mochizuki, Ben-Zvi–Frenkel

ideas.what: Passage to 𝒞/B_u (unipotent radical), adding a trivialisation φ with L^2 ≅ ω^3 and horizontality Dφ = 0.
ideas.modern_name: Theta-characteristic / square-root data in the oper description (sl2-opers as connections on J^1 of ω^{-1/2})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Beilinson–Drinfeld; Hitchin (theta characteristics in Teichmüller component)

missed.claim: Around 1972, in an algebraic relative setting X/S and in a dossier devoted to Gauss–Manin and the Cartier operator, Grothendieck works out the oper-type description of projective connections. This is a P^1-bundle 𝒞/B with flat connection and transverse section, horizontal sections = sections of 𝒰/B, plus the B_u-refinement with L^2 ≅ ω^3. It predates the algebraic/char-p treatments (Mochizuki's indigenous bundles and dormant opers, Beilinson–Drinfeld opers), but these are not credited to him.
missed.quote: Or P s'interprète comme 𝒞/B (B ⊂ PGl(1)_C, Borel) les sections loc. horizontales an sont les sections horiz. de 𝒞^an mod action de B
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows Grothendieck's interest in projective connections next to the Cartier operator and p-curvature. That combination is the core of Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory (dormant indigenous bundles) and of later work on dormant opers. The analytic content itself is Gunning's.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is essentially Gunning's indigenous bundles, in the language later standardised as opers, and is correct but classical. The modest interest is historical: Grothendieck's algebraic/relative formulation via B-reductions and the ω^3 square-root data, in a dossier tied to the Cartier operator, anticipates the context of Mochizuki's dormant opers.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'à un produit U^an × P_x^an' — the second factor is a fibre at x (P^an_x).
Lines 2–3: 'dans les morphismes vers les tr.' is more plausibly 'dans laquelle les morphismes ... P^1_x → P^1(C)'. These are trivialisations of the fibre.
Line 4: the crossed-out word is probably 'analytiques'; the insertion reads 'du' or 'des': 'donnent les germes d'applications du faisceau 𝒰'.
'Par exemple associé' is better read as 'P est associé au fibré principal (torseur) 𝒞 sur X'.
'U ⊂ Hom(X^an, P^an)' reads in the image as '𝒰 ⊂ Apphol(X^an, P^an)', i.e. holomorphic maps, consistent with the next page.
'D: ω^1 → ω^2' is better rendered 'D: ω → ω^{⊗2}' (written above as 'D: ω → ω²').
Last line: 'Revenons aux sections de 𝒞/B_u' — B_u is the unipotent radical of B (the next page's 'Π/B_n' is likely also B_u).
